finding: Unequal-link inner radius printed L1-L2 without length-order assumption.
handling: Questions use |L1-L2| explicitly or state L1>=L2.2R workspace claims are bounded to planar unrestricted joints without obstacles.

finding: Solution-count table lacks detailed geometric hypotheses; prose suggests strictly more solutions with more nonzero lengths despite two equal<=16 rows.
handling: Ask source-attributed row bounds and distinguish maximum from exact count, not a universal theorem about arbitrary6R geometry.

finding: Printed f(alpha x)=alpha x omits f on the right; fails e.g. f(x)=2x.
handling: Questions explicitly request repaired f(alpha x)=alpha f(x), with exact counterexample.

finding: Solvable=unique contradicts multi-solution and later algorithmic definition; circles/spheres as subspaces conflates arbitrary subsets with linear vector subspaces.
handling: Question contrasts definitions explicitly; unit-circle closure counterexample is supplied, not treated as a source fact.

finding: Broad all6DOF serial systems solvable/general numerical wording cannot guarantee reachable targets, convergence, uniqueness or all branches from a single initial guess.
handling: State reachable target, branch enumeration and algorithm limitations; no unconditional numerical guarantee.

finding: Text says c2 outside[-1,1] means too far away; c2<-1 actually identifies an inner unreachable region.
handling: Derive both triangle inequalities and supply separate too-close and too-far numerical counterexamples.

finding: Visible middle x/r line uses cos(gamma)cos(theta1)-sin(gamma)cos(theta1), repeating cos(theta1).
handling: Explicit repair changes the final factor to sin(theta1); derive from correct upper equations and verify forward roundtrips.

finding: Origin arbitrary theta1 omits equal-positive-link reachability condition and principal-angle modulo qualification.
handling: State equal lengths and folded elbow for the continuous origin family; never use atan2(0,0) software output as a physical constraint.

finding: Only upper triangle inequality is printed; claim that a triangle exists only for negative elbow range conflicts with the explicitly given reflected branch.
handling: Use lower and upper bounds; treat negative elbow interval as the pictured branch convention, not the only physical branch.

finding: Final line visibly prints theta3=phi-theta1+theta2, inconsistent with preceding theta1+theta2+theta3=phi.
handling: Explicitly repair to phi-theta1-theta2 and test both position and orientation; preserve defective line in citation evidence.

finding: Main J^-1 notation attempts ordinary inversion of3x2J. Flow drawing labels qdot->J->pdot and pdot->J^-1->qdot, swapped relative to qdot=Jpdot.
handling: Explicitly distinguish source drawing from corrected input/output dimensions. Use next-page pseudoinverse with feasibility assumptions.

finding: Full-rank shortcut is valid only for its stated rank case. A3x2 Jacobian does not realize arbitrary3-component desired rates; source does not discuss incompatible lateral targets.
handling: Derive no-lateral constraint and projection; distinguish least-squares output from exact physical realization and singular shortcut from general pseudoinverse.
